Subject: Post-demo: embeddings fit + next steps for semantic search evaluation

Hi Alex — thanks for a productive demo earlier. Quick recap and suggested next steps around the embeddings validation you asked for.

TL;DR: initial results look promising for 512-d embeddings using redwood-embed-512-v2; key trade-offs below and an attached CSV with the model-run outputs (embedding_eval_results.csv).

What we covered on the call
- Your goal: replace current TF-IDF pipeline for product search + FAQ matching and reduce manual tuning.
- Data: ~4M docs indexed, typical query distribution heavy on short queries (1–6 tokens).
- Success metrics: improve MRR by >= 12% and reduce false positive rate in top-5 by 20%.

Initial recommendations (fast path)
- Model: redwood-embed-512-v2 (balanced for semantic sensitivity and inference cost).
- Dimensionality: 512 dims is a good starting point; if latency/cost tight, try 256 dims with a short A/B to quantify MRR delta.
- Indexing/encoding: L2-normalize embeddings, use cosine similarity for retrieval.
- Quantization: 8-bit product quantization (PQ) on CPU-side index for archive shards; keep GPU serving in FP16 for hot shards.

Attached: embedding_eval_results.csv — contains sample query set (n=1,200), MRR, recall@10, median cosine distance per bucket, and tokenizer-length distribution.

Suggested next steps
1) Redwood runs a scoped eval over your 25k query prompt set (we can do this on your sandbox index). Deliverable: full benchmark + a prompt set with failure cases.
2) We'll instrument drift checks: monthly embedding centroid drift and daily top-k similarity decay alerts.
3) Quick M&A plan (attached) for operational handoff if you proceed.

Can you confirm a sandbox dataset upload (S3 path or a signed transfer link) and whether your team prefers 512 or wants us to include a 256-d run in the same scope?

Thanks — I’ll loop Rishi here for SLA/pricing notes once you confirm the scope.

—
Marissa Cole

Alex — thanks, great questions. Answering inline and adding a couple more operational details.

1) Repro code and seeds
We used the following reproducible pipeline (I’m pasting the key steps here; full notebook in the Drive link):
- Tokenization: Redwood tokenizer v2; seed=42 for randomized negatives sampling.
- Embedding generation: batch size 256, FP16 on A100; post-process L2-normalize.
- Similarity: cosine similarity using scipy.spatial.distance.cdist (metric="cosine"); converted to similarity via 1 - distance.
You can reproduce with the notebook link: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c/novus-embed-benchmarks

2) Drift thresholds (recommendation)
- Centroid shift (monthly): 1.5x baseline stddev on the top-5 centroid vector differences -> page ops.
- Recall@10 (weekly): drop >7% absolute from baseline -> create a regression ticket and auto-trigger a 1-week A/B to test 256 vs 512.
- Median top-k cosine similarity (daily): if median similarity for top-1 falls below baseline -0.08 -> create alert (informational) and run quick diagnostics.

Operational notes on PQ quantization and privacy
- PQ is applied at index-time as an encoding for disk-storage; the quantized vectors are not inversely mappable to raw text and are treated as derived data. Still, add a line in the M&A plan: "Quantized index shards are treated as derived embeddings and must follow existing data retention policies; access is restricted to operational roles."

3) Dimensionality A/B plan
- We will run both 256 and 512 runs over your 25k query set. Deliverables: MRR, recall@1/5/10, P@5, index size delta, average query latency at target QPS, and cost per 1M queries estimate.

Pricing/SLA note (Rishi)
- Rishi: we expect this scoped eval to be a 3–4 day effort on Redwood side; please confirm the recommended commit level for a free scoped bench vs paid PoC.

If that all looks good I’ll provision the sandbox and share an upload token.

—
Marissa
